Measuring the APRPD
text:
Ideally the fetal spine should be at 12 o’clock position / 6 o’clock position 
In postnatal patients the AP RPD should be measured with the patient in prone position.The prone position tends to increase the width of the pelvis compared to the supine position. However in case this is not feasible, it should be documented that the measurement has been done in supine position. Subsequent measurements in serial USGs should be taken in the same patient position.

title: In Antenatal scans:-
text: Visualisation of ureter(s) is considered abnormal irrespective of the ureteric calibre

title: In postnatal patients:-
text:
“Normal ureters are distended by urine, and visualizing this does not mean that the ureter is abnormally dilated”
Ureters should be evaluated in both prevoid as well as postvoid states
Distal ureter calibre >4 mm is considered abnormal

text:

Abnormal (Megacystis/Thickened wall/Ureterocoele)

title: In the first trimester, megacystis is defined as a urinary bladder measuring greater than 7 mm in diameter
